intro: If you want to sleep in a Thai teak house on the river, wake to paddle boats drifting past your room, and walk a few minutes to Amphawa Floating Market, Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa is the name that comes up most for a riverside Amphawa stay · This 4-star resort lines Rattanakosin-style teak houses along the Mae Klong River in the heart of Amphawa · Guests remember it for its leafy Thai-house atmosphere, two swimming pools and the riverside Suphannika Spa · Standard rooms start from about THB 2,300/night, with villas and pool suites rising with size and privacy.

body.html: Amphawa is a Mae Klong riverside district that Bangkok can reach in just over an hour, and its riverside stays run from shophouse homestays to full resorts · Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa is one of the largest and best-kept 4-star properties in the area · Open since around 2006 and substantially renovated around 2024, it lines clusters of Rattanakosin-style Thai teak houses along the river and through the gardens — roughly 59 rooms and villas in all, split into a Thai Village zone and a Tropical Villa zone, a mid-size resort that still feels private.

The part everyone talks about is the riverside Thai-house atmosphere you rarely find in a modern resort · Teak houses with Thai-style roofs, wooden walkways linking the buildings, coconut palms and garden ponds give the whole place the feel of a well-kept old Thai village · There are two outdoor pools to cool off in, a pool bar, and Suphannika Spa for Thai massage and treatments by the water · Many reviews say morning coffee by the river, or watching the paddle boats pass at dusk, is their favourite part of staying here.

"Sleeping in a teak house by the river, opening the door in the morning to water and paddle boats, then a five-minute walk to Amphawa Floating Market — the real Amphawa feeling without being squeezed into a shophouse."

Rooms come in several grades across two zones · The Thai Village runs from Superior and Deluxe up to Super Deluxe and Pool Suites, while the Tropical Villa zone offers standalone villas such as Prime Villa, Pool Villa and two-bedroom Grand Villas for families · Every room is a teak house with a Thai feel, air-con, a flat-screen TV, fridge and a private balcony or veranda, many looking onto the garden or river · Most reviews praise the good-looking rooms, the atmosphere and the attentive staff · The common observation is that this is a resort with some age — a few spots and furnishings are starting to show wear despite the partial renovation.

For food, the main outlet is Sabannga, a riverside Thai restaurant with live music on some evenings, serving Thai food and seafood over the water · Breakfast earns praise for its setting and staff, though a few reviews would like more variety · A big plus of the location is that you can easily eat out at Amphawa Floating Market — grilled seafood, Thai sweets and canalside snacks — so you don't have to eat every meal at the resort.

On scores, Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa reviews well and consistently · The average across real-guest platforms sits around 8.4 out of 10, and it ranks among the top stays in Amphawa on TripAdvisor · Repeated praise goes to the riverside location in the heart of Amphawa, the Thai-house atmosphere and the gracious, professional staff · The common gripes are about the resort's age, maintenance of a few areas such as the pools and furniture, and spa pricing that runs on the high side.

To be straight about it, this is not a brand-new boutique resort where everything is pristine, and its appeal was never about being new · The real draw is simple: you sleep in a Thai teak house on the Mae Klong River, within walking distance of Amphawa Floating Market · Standard rooms start around THB 2,300 on weekdays, rising on weekends when the market is at its busiest · If you expect a slick, modern resort in every corner, look elsewhere · But for a genuine riverside Thai-house atmosphere, market on your doorstep, and a pool and spa to unwind in, Baan Amphawa does the job well.

A tip from reading plenty of reviews here: if you want the full atmosphere, take a room or villa that looks onto, or sits right on, the river, because the river view is the whole reason people come · The cheaper inner rooms look onto the garden instead · If you're visiting on a weekend or long holiday, book ahead — Amphawa is a favourite escape for Bangkok and the riverside rooms go fast · And don't forget to ask the resort about the evening firefly boat tour, a highlight no Amphawa visitor should miss.

highlights.title: Thai teak houses on the river
highlights.text: Clusters of Rattanakosin-style teak houses line the Mae Klong River and gardens, a Thai-village feel you rarely find in a modern resort.

highlights.title: Walk to Amphawa Floating Market
highlights.text: Right in the heart of Amphawa — walk out for grilled seafood, Thai sweets and the canalside market without driving anywhere.

highlights.text: Two outdoor pools, a pool bar, and the riverside Suphannika Spa for Thai massage and unwinding after a day exploring.

honestSummary: Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa is one of the most authentically Amphawa riverside stays — Thai teak houses on the Mae Klong River, a walk to the floating market, with pools and a spa to relax in · It isn't a brand-new resort and shows some age in places, but for an Amphawa trip where you want the genuine riverside Thai-house feel, it lands just right.
honestChecks: If you're here mainly for the riverside atmosphere — the cheaper inner garden-view rooms won't give you the feeling you came for → pay up for a river-view or riverside room or villa and it's better value.
If you expect a slick, modern resort in every corner — this is a teak property with some age; its appeal is Thai atmosphere, not newness → set expectations accordingly and you'll enjoy the charm.
If you're coming on a busy market weekend — riverside rooms sell out fast and the area gets crowded → book ahead, and if you want quiet, consider a weekday instead.

tips.title: Choose a river-view or riverside room

tips.title: Explore the floating market in the evening
tips.body: Amphawa Floating Market is busiest from afternoon to night on Fri–Sun. Walk out from the resort for grilled seafood and Thai sweets.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa, Samut Songkhram

faq.q: Where is Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa and how do I get there?
faq.a: It sits on the Mae Klong River, Kaewfah Rd, Bang Kaphom, Amphawa District, Samut Songkhram · It's just over an hour's drive from Bangkok with free parking · It's right in the heart of Amphawa, a few minutes' walk from Amphawa Floating Market.

faq.q: How much does Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Superior rooms start from about THB 2,300/night on weekdays · The range runs from Deluxe and Pool Suites up to standalone villas like Prime Villa and two-bedroom Grand Villas for families · Prices rise on weekends — compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Can you really walk to Amphawa Floating Market?
faq.a: Yes · The resort is right in the heart of Amphawa, about a 5-minute walk to Amphawa Floating Market · The market is busiest from afternoon to night on Fri–Sun, with grilled seafood, Thai sweets and the evening firefly boat pier nearby.

faq.q: Is it good for families or couples?
faq.a: Both · There are riverside Thai teak houses, two pools and two-bedroom villas for families · The leafy Thai-house atmosphere suits couples wanting the genuine Amphawa feel, and families who want a riverside base within walking distance of the market.

faq.q: What are the review scores like, and what are the downsides?
faq.a: The average across real-guest reviews is around 8.4 out of 10, ranking among the top stays in Amphawa on TripAdvisor · Common praise: the riverside location, the Thai-house atmosphere and the gracious staff · The downsides are the resort's age, with some spots and furniture showing wear, and spa pricing on the high side.
